whatThisIs: Source pins and digests for every byte this regression check compares. Nothing here is produced by this repository except the runner: the pinned verifier modules are toy bytes, and the Genesis fixture is Genesis bytes. Each digest was recomputed from the file on disk in this tree and cross-checked against the blob or manifest it came from.

pinnedContract.why: This is the revision aumara-xyz/aukora-genesis vendors today as vendor/receipt-v3, pinned by its own upstream-receipt-v3.json at this exact commit. Snapshotting it here makes the pinned acceptance behaviour checkable without a sibling checkout of Genesis, and without this repository's current toy/ being able to stand in for it: the runner imports these bytes under an isolated PYTHONPATH, and this tree is not on the path.

files.note: The one module whose closed-set rules differ between the two revisions. Its COMP_BASE is the 5-field composition set.

pinnedContract.closureNote: receipt.py imports diamond.ed25519, diamond.hexutil and diamond.jcs; those import the standard library only. cold_verify.py is deliberately NOT snapshotted: the runner compares the receipt.py seam directly, and a CLI wrapper would add a second surface without adding a comparison.
pinnedContract.note: Vendored bytes from aukora-toy (now aukora-diamond) at c512d0c, repackaged under this repository's renamed package. `upstreamSha256` is the digest at c512d0c; `sha256` is the digest of the vendored file here. For four of the five files they are identical. receipt.py differs in exactly three lines — its internal `from toy.X import` statements become `from diamond.X import` so the vendored package matches its new name — which is +12 bytes. That is the whole delta, and it is checkable: `diff <(git show c512d0c:toy/receipt.py) pinned/diamond/receipt.py` prints those three lines and nothing else.

fixture.why: A real aukora-receipt/v3-genesis receipt produced by the Genesis composition gate itself, committed in Genesis as a public fixture. It is the concrete specimen this check is about: a receipt that exists today and whose acceptance changes between the two revisions.

files.note: Digest matches the fixtures[] entry in Genesis vendor/receipt-v3/upstream-receipt-v3.json exactly. Its composition block carries the 5-field set.
PUBLIC key only. No issuer secret key exists in this tree, in Genesis, or in this comparison.

experienceFixture.why: The kind that court sealed, in the two shapes its producer emits. The matrix carries rows for it: what each consumer HERE does when the document is handed to it. Both documents are advisory and unsigned - grantsAuthority is false and there is no signature field - so no verifier of authority can reach a signature on them.
experienceFixture.note: Derived, not vendored by hand: the bytes come from that court's own ExperienceStore at the commit above, serialized as JSON with sorted keys because its records live in memory. The full commit is pinned rather than a short SHA, which is a display convenience whose length varies with the size of the repository.

files.note: ExperienceStore.put(): a stored record with its content-addressed source.
ExperienceStore.recall(): a reply citing records; the answer is never a grant.

comparisonBytesProducedHere.note: The re-signed variants are generated at run time by the runner, not committed. The signing seed is a fixed constant that is written in the runner source and is therefore public and worthless: it exists so the signature over the comparison bytes is a real Ed25519 signature that this check can reproduce, and so no secret material is ever stored.
comparisonBytesProducedHere.whyReSignedVariants: The committed Genesis fixture cannot be mutated into the newer shape without invalidating its signature, and re-signing it would require the Genesis issuer secret, which does not exist here. A throwaway-key copy of the same document isolates the ONE variable under test: the composition closed set. Signature validity is held constant across variants so a refusal cannot be explained by a bad signature.

notDone: Genesis is not modified, and its verifier is not repinned.
Neither schema is loosened: the current revision is compared unmodified, and so are the pinned bytes.
No signature is relabelled and no kind string is rewritten. Changing only kind is a separate, already-tested refusal (scripts/verify-v3-genesis-acceptance.py arm 4).
